title: 17 · kirata · The Hunter and the Prince
lines: The greatest archer alive once lost a fight to a stranger in the woods.
He was never happier to lose.
Arjuna needed a weapon no man could give him.
So he went to the mountains to pray to Shiva.
And a second arrow hit it at the same instant.
A hunter stepped out of the trees.
The hunter swallowed every arrow like rain.
He swung his bow. The hunter took it.
He used his fists. He was thrown like a child.
Arjuna crawled back to his little clay lingam,
and laid a garland on it.
The garland was around the hunter's neck.
The stranger's feathers became a crescent moon.
When you lose to God, you have won. That is sadhana.
